title: Token Ledger Studio — ideation & wireframe grooming
body:
Context:
This doc collects early ideation for a compact, developer-friendly view into per-invocation token cost and latency called "Token Ledger Studio". Goal: give engineers a single pane to debug unexpected token spikes, latency cliffs, and routing/fallback behavior without having to stitch together traces + billing reports.

Why different (working hypothesis):
- Current token dashboards are aggregate-first (heatmaps, totals). Need a reverse view: start from a single invocation and expand outward (why did this call cost 3x?).
- Desire a ledger metaphor: chronological, line-item bookkeeping for every token that contributed cost/latency (prefix cache hits, KV misses, quantization path changes).
- Combine cost attribution with causal signals: model variant changes, routing fallback, batching delays.

Key UX primitives to explore:
1) Invocation Row (compact): one-line summary for each invocation in a selected time window.
   - columns: time, invocation id, model variant, cost (USD), latency (p95/p50), token count, route (region/pool), outcome (ok/timeout/fallback).
   - affordance: expand chevron -> opens Ledger Card.

2) Ledger Card (token chronicle): chronological scroll of token events for the invocation. Think of a financial ledger with debit/credit lines but applied to tokens and micro-latency events.
   - rows can be collapsed/expanded by token group (prompt / system / user / generated / function-call).
   - each row fields: token text (truncated), token type, token index, cost contribution, observed latency delta, cache_status (hit/miss), kernel_path (float16/int8/kv-optimized), KV-cache-size at time t, batching_group_id.
   - hover state surfaces: full token text, decoder step metrics, relevant log lines.

3) Waterfall + Sparkline hybrid: to the right of the Ledger Card, a tight waterfall shows cumulative latency with micro-breakdowns (queueing, kernel compute, network, fallback). Underneath a sparkline of per-token compute time to see spikes.

4) Playback scrubber: user can scrub along token index to see how the model generated text over time, and how cost/latency change as different tokens are produced. Useful for reproducing hallucination or runaway generation cost patterns.

5) Diff vs Baseline: select a baseline model version or quantization profile and diff the invocation ledger against it. Highlight tokens or groups with the largest delta in cost or latency.

6) Anomaly flags and auto-suggestions: ledger auto-suggests likely causes (e.g., "unexpected suffix: long generated function call", "KV eviction occurred", "routing fallback to 1/2 precision"). These are heuristics surfaced with links to matching traces or replay keys.

Wireframe notes (sketches, rough):
- Top bar: time filter, search (invocation id / user id / session), sample rate toggle (show examples vs all).
- Left column: invocation list. Center: expanded Ledger Card. Right column: waterfall + quick diffs + suggested actions (replay, pin, create alert).
- Compact mode: ledger card overlays on top of list with 3-line summary and mini-sparkline.

ASCII layout (for quick mental model):
[ Time filter | Search | Sample rate ]
--------------------------------------------------------
| Invocations (list) | Ledger Card (expanded) | Details |
|  - 10:12:02 id=..  |  [token ledger rows]    | waterfall|
|  - 10:12:11 id=..  |  [playback scrubber]    | suggestions|
--------------------------------------------------------

Interaction ideas / microinteractions:
- Ctrl/Cmd+click tokens to pin multiple tokens and run a mini-diff against baseline.
- Right-click on ledger row to open raw logs or copy token text.
- Hover heatmap on sparkline to show nearest token index and corresponding token row highlight.
- Keyboard nav: j/k move between invocations; enter expands ledger; left/right scrubs tokens.

Data & backend considerations (notes for infra/serving team):
- Need per-token telemetry emitted by runtime: cost_estimate, compute_time_ms, cache_hit (bool), kernel_variant. Can be batched in traces or shipped as separate token telemetry events.
- Storage: keep recent full ledgers hot (30 days) and sample long tail; provide a fast lookup by invocation id.
- Privacy: mask PII tokens by default; token preview shows only first 6 chars + ellipsis unless user has proper role.
- Cost calculations: server-side canonical USD conversion with rounding; show breakdown by unit (compute, memory, kv-io).

Backlog grooming (candidate stories & estimates):
- P0: Invocation list + expand to simple ledger rows (no playback). ~5 d (FE: 3d, BE: 2d).
- P1: Waterfall micro-breakdown + sparkline per-token. ~6 d (FE: 4d, BE: 2d).
- P1: Playback scrubber (token-index timeline control). ~5 d (FE: 4d, BE: 1d delivered via existing traces).
- P2: Diff vs baseline (UI + compute diffs). ~4 d (FE: 2d, BE: 2d).
- P2: Auto-suggestion heuristics (initial set of 6 rules). ~3 d (ML heuristics + UI).
- P3: Pinboard / saved investigations + link to alert create. ~3 d.

Acceptance criteria (for beta):
- Given an invocation id, user can expand ledger and see token rows with cost and latency for >90% of sampled invocations (sample rate 1% baseline).
- Playback scrubber shows token index and highlights corresponding ledger row within 200ms of interaction.
- Anomaly suggestions surface at least one actionable hint for >30% of flagged invocations in initial heuristic set.

Open questions / decisions needed (for next sync):
- Sampling policy: show every invocation vs sampled; default sample rate to balance cost. How to allow customers to set sampling per project?
- Retention SLA: how long do we keep full token ledgers in hosted offering? 30 days vs 90 days? Price tiers?
- PII policy: auto-mask vs role-based unmask. Legal input required.
- Should we expose raw tokens to SRE/eng by default or require an opt-in?
- How to integrate with existing trace ids (X-Trace header) so SREs can jump into perf traces?

Next steps / owner action items:
- Riley: prototype quick HTML wireframe (low-fi) and post to Figma for internal review — due 2026-01-08.
- Aisha: sync with serving-runtime to validate per-token telemetry feasibility and event schema — due 2025-12-05.
- Marco: draft retention and masking options for legal + pricing — due 2025-12-10.
- Samir: create JIRA epics for P0 & P1 and link to this doc (JIRA keys to be added).

Quick notes from 2026-01-12 team huddle (raw):
- Clara: suggested a "cost bucket" column (prompt vs expensive generator vs function call) — sounds useful for high level triage.
- Riley: we should avoid exposing full token strings in search; search should index token hashes + context snippets.
- Marco: ask billing team about clear USD per-token lines to avoid mismatch from per-model unit pricing.

Rough prototypes attached: (textual descriptions below, actual frames in Figma link above)
- Frame A (debug-first): large Ledger Card, right column waterfall, minimal list. Use for SRE/solutions onboarding.
- Frame B (investigate-first): left list enriched with tags (+anomalies), quick actions to pin and export. Use for product owners.
- Frame C (compact): overlay ledger on rows for quick spot checks in tenant dashboards.

Closing thought: name is intentionally centric on the ledger/studio metaphor to set expectations: this is a place to do clean accounting and iterative investigation (pin, replay, diff). Long term we can fold in alerts, SLA cost forecasts, and per-route optimizers.

References / inspirations:
- internal: token-playback-scrubber-ux-notes (see linked artifacts)
- external inspirations: profiler timelines (chrome devtools), financial transaction ledgers, database WAL viewers.
